Definition: to equalize, i.e. straighten (intransitive or transitive); figuratively, to compose
BiblicalUsage: The word is to make straight what is crooked, or to set in order. The Preacher says that which is crooked cannot be made straight, and asks who can make straight what God hath made crooked; and he says the Preacher set in order many proverbs.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that only God straightens what is crooked, and the wise man knows the limits of his own ordering.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
